react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set drives a convergent perturbation across two tightly coupled metabolic axes: one centered on the methionine cycle and trans-sulfuration pathway, and a second centered on arachidonic acid–derived eicosanoid synthesis. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR 1.2×10⁻¹³), MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 3.4×10⁻⁷), and Mummichog m/z-direct activity (p = 0.016) — KEGG:hsa00270 Methionine Metabolism emerges as the top cross-paradigm winner, supported by S-adenosyl-L-methionine, L-homocysteine, L-methionine, choline, adenosine, L-glutamic acid, and cysteic acid. The methionine cycle feeds into the trans-sulfuration route where cysteic acid (the direct oxidation product of cysteine) appears, consistent with oxidative stress or accelerated cysteine catabolism in the treatment condition. Simultaneously, Mummichog independently recovers arachidonic acid metabolism (p = 0.016) as a co-hit, anchored by 15(S)-HETE and 8(S)-HPETE. The concurrent elevation of these eicosanoid intermediates suggests increased 15-lipoxygenase and/or 12-lipoxygenase flux. Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260, FDR 3.7×10⁻¹⁹ via RaMP) is also robustly enriched, implicating threonine and choline as upstream amino-group donors that replenish the methionine cycle. Lipoic acid (KEGG:C16241) appears in the glycerophospholipid and lipoate-metabolism modules, consistent with its role as a cofactor forpyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, enzymes that intersect with the glutamate and methionine nodes. The multi-paradigm convergence on hsa00270 as the consensus winner, with driver metabolites verified in the metabolites_hit rosters of all three tools, establishes methionine dysregulation as the primary biological signal in this dataset.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set produces a convergent signal across Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) and Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270 / KEGG:map00270), with the methionine axis emerging as the primary driver. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism first (FDR 3.75e-19, 8 metabolites hit) and Methionine Metabolism rank 5 (FDR 1.19e-13, 6 metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms Methionine Metabolism (hsa00270, p=3.36e-07, 4 metabolites hit including S-adenosyl-L-methionine, L-homocysteine, L-methionine, L-cysteic acid) and additionally identifies the folate one-carbon pool pathway (hsa00670, p=3.36e-07, 5 metabolites hit). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently hits Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism and Methionine and cysteine metabolism as its top-ranked pathways (p=0.014, overlap=8). The convergent enrichment across all three paradigms establishes Methionine Metabolism as the central biological signal. Driver metabolites S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019) and L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155) appear in the metabolites_hit lists of every tool. L-Threonine (KEGG:C00188) and choline (KEGG:C00114) bridge the glycine/serine/threonine and methionine axes. 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) and 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) appear only in mummichog, indicating他们是lipid-derived signals detectable by m/z but below the ORA threshold.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set produces a convergent signal across Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) and Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270 / KEGG:map00270), with the methionine axis emerging as the primary driver. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism first (FDR 3.75e-19, 8 metabolites hit) and Methionine Metabolism rank 5 (FDR 1.19e-13, 6 metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms Methionine Metabolism (hsa00270, p=3.36e-07, 4 metabolites hit including S-adenosyl-L-methionine, L-homocysteine, L-methionine, L-cysteic acid) and additionally identifies the folate one-carbon pool pathway (hsa00670, p=3.36e-07, 5 metabolites hit). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently hits Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism and Methionine and cysteine metabolism as its top-ranked pathways (p=0.014, overlap=8). The convergent enrichment across all three paradigms establishes Methionine Metabolism as the central biological signal. Driver metabolites S-adenosyl-L-methionine (KEGG:C00019) and L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00155) appear in the metabolites_hit lists of every tool. L-Threonine (KEGG:C00188) and choline (KEGG:C00114) bridge the glycine/serine/threonine and methionine axes. 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) and 8(S)-HPETE (KEGG:C14823) appear only in mummichog, indicating他们是lipid-derived signals detectable by m/z but below the ORA threshold.
